for quarantine inspection. Vessels arriving at the entrance between sunset
and io p. in. will be boarded and inspected unless specific request to the contrary
is made by the vessel or her agent prior to her being sighted.

clauses.label: Section 31.
clauses.text:
Section 31. On arrival, the following papers must be ready for immediate
delivery to the boarding party, for inspection or taking up as the case may be:
,. Panama Canal Certificate (Panama Canal Form 4400-1).
2. National Register.

3. Passenger List (4 copies) P. C. Form 18-2 (white). (Not applicable to
men-of-war or to vessels carrying large bodies of troops or contract
laborers. In such cases, state aggregate number, nationality, occupa-
tioni, port of embarkation and final destination.)
4. Crew List (2 copies) P. C. Form 159 (Not applicable to men-of-war.State number on board.)
5. Clearance from last port.
6. Bill of health.
7. Ship information sheet (P. C. Form 4398-15).
8. Manifest of local cargo (3 copies) .

9. Cargo declaration (P. C. Form 4363), or complete manifest. (Vessels
transiting only.) A manifest so submitted may have the names of
consignor and consignee deleted.
to. Descriptive list of Chinese on hoard (2 copies) P. C. Form 1400.
I I. Store List.
12. Statement of fuel account (for vessels in ballast).
13. Praticlue.
14. Fumigation certificate (not over 6 months old).
15. Birth and death certificates, if any occurred during voyage.
16. Orders for supplies.

clauses.label: Section 32.
clauses.text:
Section 32. A vessel's Panama Can~al Certificate may be taken up by the
admeasurer and retained at the Canal, if necessary, until the vessel's next visit.

clauses.label: Section 33.
clauses.text:
Section 33. Outgoing vessels should receive a clearance and bill of health
before departure and must deliver the following papers to the Canal authorities:
i. Passeiig~r list (2 copies) P. C. Form 14-I (buff). This form may be
submitted with the following declaration on the face: "List of passen-
gers same as incoming, with these exceptions (noting exceptions)."

2. Manifest of cargo taken aboard at Canal Zone ports. If none taken, a
statement to that effect.

clauses.label: Section 34.
clauses.text:
Section 34. Vessels shall be cleared by the Port Captain but he shall not
issue a clearance until he has ascertained:I

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) That the required documents and statistical data in regard to vessel,
cargo, and passengers have been furnished by the master of the vessel, or that
satisfactory arrangements have been made to furnish them through an agency
on the Isthmus.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) That all tolls and other bills for services and supplies furnished by The
Panama Canal or Panama Railroad have been paid, or that their payment has
been secured.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) That the vessel has complied with the quarantine and immigration laws
and regulations of the Canal Z'one.
4

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) That the laws and regulations governing the shipment and discharge
of seamen, and for the protection of seamen, have been complied with.

clauses.label: Section 35.
clauses.text:
Section 35. Manifests, lists and statements required above shall be sworn
to by the master or agent of the vessel. B,.arding officers are authorized to
acknowledge depositions and oaths.

clauses.label: Section 36.
clauses.text:
Section 36. Vessels shall, at all times, when under way in Canal waters,
when passing through the locks, or moored temporarily in transit through the
Canal, keep a full watch on deck and in the engine room, in the same manner
in which they are kept at sea.
Section 37 Wheni a vessel is entering or leaving a lock, getting under way,
anchoring, shifting berth, or is under way in Gaillard Cut, the captain or master
shall be on the bridge and all other officers shall be at their regular stations.
Deck officers shall, in addition, remain at their stations while the vessel is in
the locks.

clauses.label: Section 38.
clauses.text:
Section 38. In addition to the regular engineer officers of the watch, the
chief engineer of a ship shall remain on duty in the engine room during the
approach to and while passing through the locks, arid until the lockage shall
have been completed and the vessel is clear of the lock walls. He shall also be
in the engine room when the vessel is passing through Gaillard Cut, and in getting
under way, anchoring or shifting berth. A full head of steam is required on
such occasions.

clauses.label: Section 39.
clauses.text:
Section 39. While a vessel is under way in Canal waters, no one shall be
allowed on the bridge or in the pilot house except the pilot and other representa-
tives of the Canal, the master, and such officers and crew of the ship as may
be necessary for her management, direction and safety. Under no condition
will any passenger or any other unauthorized person be allowed on the bridge
ar in the pilot house.

clauses.label: Section 40.
clauses.text:
Section 40. ?Masters shall require all passengers and other persons not
engaged in working the ship to keep well clear of bitts, chocks, winches and
other gear being used in this connection. The Panama Canal will not be respon-
sible for injuries to persons violating this rule.

clauses.label: Section 41.
clauses.text:
Section 41. Before beginning the passage of the Canal, vessels will be
required to have hawsers, lines, and fenders ready for passing through the locks,
for warping, towing, or mooring as the case may be; avid will have both anchors
ready for letting go. The master shall assure himself, by actual test, of the
readiness of his main engines, steering gear, engine room telegraphs, rudder
and engine indicators and anchors. During the passage, at all times while the
vessel is under way or moored against the lock walls, her deck winches, cap-
stans or other power for handling lines, as well as her mooring bitts, deck chocks,
cleats, hawse pipes, etc., shall be ready for handling ship, to the exclusion of
all other work.

clauses.label: Section 42.
clauses.text:
Section 42. The Panama Canal is not responsible for damage to any pro-
trusion beyond the ship's side, permanent or otherwise; the latter must be
rigged in before transit or going alongside a dock, the former must be protected
by adequate fenders.

clauses.label: Section 43.
clauses.text:
Section 43. At least one boat for handling lines shall be kept ready for
lowering.
Section 44 When necessary, additional rudder area will be required to he
fitted before a ship enters.
Section 45 All vessels must be properly trimmed before entering. A
vessel is considered as properly trimmed when she is on at- even keel as to list
and has a slight drag. A vessel is never properly trimmed when she has a list
or is down b~y the head or has an excessive drag. If a vessel arrives at the Canal
not properly trimmed, and it is impossible to remedy this condition, the vessel
will be takenx through, but the Canal will not be responsible for the safe transit
of a vessel that is not properly trimmed, as given above, or is overloaded to such
an extent as to effect her maneuvering qualities.

clauses.label: Section 46.
clauses.text:
Section 46. In all cases the pilot boarding anl incoming vessel shall be the
judge as to whether or not she is ready. for transit, pending reference of the matter
to the Port Captain.

Section 47 A vessel carrying a deck load shal have it so arranged that it
will be clear of all chocks, bitts and other gear used in locking.

clauses.label: Section 48.
clauses.text:
Section 48. All sailing craft, vessels whose machinery may be in bad
condition or disabled, and vessels without motive power, must be towed through
the Canal, for which service an additional charge will be imposed.
Section 49 When passing through the locks, vessels will habitually be
towed by Canal equipment. In exceptional instances, as when such equipment
is not available, or in case of very small vessels, the vessel's own motive power
may be used, but the crew and officers will be expected to render such assistance
as may be necessary to supplement the lock force. A vessel when being towed
through the locks may, when necessary, use her iTain engines in the ahead motion
only when starting out of a chamber. Except in an emergency, the main engines
will never be used to stop such a ship after entering a chamber.

clauses.label: Section 5o.
clauses.text:
Section 5o. The Governor of The Panama Canal is authorized to issue orders
from time to time regulating the procedure in passing vessels through the locks.

clauses.label: Section 51j.
clauses.text:
Section 51j. Masters of vessels will not allow anyone to take passage on their
ships while passing through the Canal, except the ship's officers, crew, and duly
accredited passengers, and such officials and other persons as may be designated
by Canal authorities.

clauses.label: Section 52.
clauses.text:
Section 52. If any defect in any part of a vessel be discovered while in
transit, of such a serious nature that it might interfere with the further passage
of the veessl, the vessel shall stop, and, if practicable, be anchored or moored at
the first available place. A full report shall immediately be made to the Port
Captain.

clauses.label: Section 53.
clauses.text:
Section 53. The Canal authorities may require any vessel to take a tug
through the Cut, on approaching the locks, or in any other part of the Canal,
when, in their opinion, it may be necessary to insure the safety of the vessel and
the Canal.
Section 54 Should a vessel steer badly, the captain or master should so
report and request the services of a tug to assist him through the Cut, or when-
ever a vessel is liable to become unmanageable for any reason. she shall imnmedi-
ately, through the pilot, request the assistance of a tug. In either case the
tug service is chargeable to the ship.

clauses.label: Section 55.
clauses.text:
Section 55. No firearms of any kind shall be discharged while in transit
through the Canal or in Canal waters.

clauses.label: Section 56.
clauses.text:
Section 56. Pilots, extra deck hands, and other authorized persons on duty,
belonging to the Canal Service, shall be subsisted without charge while on board
vessels in transit.

clauses.label: Section 57.
clauses.text:
Section 57. No vessel, company or individual will be authorized to maintain
or operate permanently any tugs, launches, lighters, or floating equipment of any
kind within Canal waters without authority from the Governor.

clauses.label: Section 58.
clauses.text:
Section 58. Except by special authority of the Governor and on a pass from
the Port Captain's office, in each individual case, passengers will not be allowed
to embark upon or disembark from vessels in the locks.

4. RULES OF THE ROAD, WHISTLE AND OTHER SIGNALS AND
SPEED REGULATIONS.

clauses.label: Section 59.
clauses.text:
Section 59. In the following rules every steam vessel which is under sail
and not under steam, is considered a sailing vessel; and every vessel under its
own motive power, whether under sail or not, is to be considered a steam vessel.

clauses.label: Section 6o.
clauses.text:
Section 6o. The words " steam vessel " and " steamer " shall include every
vessel propelled by machinery.
Section 6 u. A vessel is under way, within the meaning of these rules, when
she is not at anchor, moored, or aground.

clauses.label: Section 62.
clauses.text:
Section 62. Risk of collision cr.n, when circumstances permit, be determined
by carefully watching the bearings of an approaching vessel by compass, or
otherwise; if the courses be converging and the bearing does not appreciably
change, such risk should be deemed to -exist.
6

clauses.label: Section 63.
clauses.text:
Section 63. Steam vessels shall be provided with an efficient whistle or
siren, sounded by steam or some substitute for steam, so placed that the sound
may not be intercepted by any obstruction, and sailing vessels of 20 gross tons
or upward with an efficient foghorn; both shall be supplied with an efficient bell.

clauses.label: Section 64.
clauses.text:
Section 64. The words " motor boat" include every vessel propelled by
machinery and not more than 65 feet in length, except tug boats propelled by
steam.

clauses.label: Section 65.
clauses.text:
Section 65. Motor boats shall be divided into classes as follows, according
to the length, which shall be measured from end to end :
Class I. Less than 26 feet.
Class II. 26 feet or over, but less than 40o feet.
Class III. 40 feet or over, but less than 65 feet.

clauses.label: Section 66.
clauses.text:
Section 66. All motor boats shall be provided with a whistle or other
mechanical sound-producing device, capable of making a blast of at least two
seconds' duration, and, in addition, Classes II and III shall be provided with an
efficient foghorn and fog bell, the latter to be at least eight inches across the
mo~uth.

clauses.label: Section 67.
clauses.text:
Section 67. A short blast of the whistle shall mean a blast of about one
second's duration, and a prolonged blast of the whistle shall mean a blast of
from four to six seconds' duration.

clauses.label: Section 68.
clauses.text:
Section 68. One short blast of the whistle signifies intention of or assent
to the steamer first giving the signal to direct course to her own starboard,
except when two steamers are approaching each other at right angles or obliquely,
when it signifies intention of steamer which is to starboard of the other to hold
course and speed.

clauses.label: Section 69.
clauses.text:
Section 69. Two short blasts of the whistle signify intention of or assent to
the steamer first giving the signal to direct course to her own port, except when
steamers are approaching each other at right angles or obliquely, when the
signal signifies desire of or assent to steamer which is to the port of the other to
cross the bow of the steamer to starboard.

clauses.label: Section 70.
clauses.text:
Section 70. Three short blasts of the whistle shall mean: "My engines are
going full speed astern", and when vessels are in sight of one another a steam
vessel under way whose engines are going full speed astern shall indicate that
fact by three short blasts of the whistle.

clauses.label: Section 71.
clauses.text:
Section 71. If, when vessels are approaching each other, either vessel fails
to understand the course or intention of the other, from any cause, the vessel so
iii doubt shall immediately signify the same by making the danger signal, namely:
Several short and rapid blasts, not fewer than four, on the steam whistle.

clauses.label: Section 72.
clauses.text:
Section 72. Whenever the danger signal is given, the engines of both
steamers shall be stopped and backed until the headway of the steamers has been
fully checked; nor shall the engines of either steamer be again started ahead
until the steamers can safely pass each other, and the proper signals for passing
have been given, answered, and understood.

clauses.label: Section 73.
clauses.text:
Section 73. Steam vessels are forbidden to use what has become technically
known as " cross signals", that is, answering one whistle with two, and answering
two whistles with one. In all cases, and under all circumstances, a pilot receiv-
ing either of the whistle signals provided in these rules, which for any reason
he deems injudicious to comply with, instead of answering it with a cross signal,
shall at once sound the danger signal and observe the rule applying thereto.

clauses.label: Section 74.
clauses.text:
Section 74. Tlhe whistle signals for passing shall be given and answered
by vessels, in compliance with these rules, not only when meeting head on, or
nearly so, but at all times when the vessels are in sight of each other, when
passing or meeting at a distance within a half mile of each other, and whether
passing to starboard or port.

clauses.label: Section 75.
clauses.text:
Section 75. The whistle signals provided in the rules for steam vessels
meeting, passing, or overtaking, are never to be used except when steamers
are in sight of each other, and the course and position of each can be determined
in the daytime by a sight of the vessel itself, or at night by seeing its lights,
except in cases hereafter mentioned, where vessels are approaching a turn in

the Canal. In fog, mist, o,: heavy rainstorms, when vessels can not see each
other, fog signals only must be given.
Section -6. When steam vessels are approaching each other head on, or
nearly so, it shall be the duty of each to pass on the port side of the other; and
either vessel shall give as a signal of her intention one short and distinct blast
of her whistle, and thereupon they shall pass on the port side of each other.
But if their courses be so far to starboard of each other as not to be considered
as meeting head on, either vessel shall immediately give two short, distinct
blasts of her whistle, which the other vessel shall answer promptly with two
similar blasts, and they shall pass to starboard of each other; but vessels going
in opposite directions, in transit through the Canal shall make it an invariable
rule to pass to port of each other, unless there be some special reason to the
con trarv.
Section 77.Wnhen two steamers sight each other going in opposite direc-
tions, they shall, when within a mile of each other, be slowed to dead slow speed
and each kept on its starboard side of the channel until passed and clear.

clauses.label: Section 78.
clauses.text:
Section 78. Vessels other than Canal craft proceeding in the same direc-
tion shall not pass each other in the Canal, except between buoys i 7 and 78,
in Gatun Lake, and then only on advice of the pilot to do so.

clauses.label: Section 79.
clauses.text:
Section 79. Self-propelled Canal craft, at work on their stations or under
way, will give way and leave the center of the channels clear to sea-going vessels
in transit; nothing in this rule shall be construed to warrant a violation of the
Rules of the Road, but shall be interpreted to mean that tugs, launches, and
small self-propelled craft shall keep close to the side of the Canal and out of
mid-channel when large vessels are passing, whenever practicable, without
involving any danger to themselves.
Section So. The foregoing applies only to cases where vessels are meeting
end on, or nearly so, in such manner as to involve risk of collision.
Section 8 1. Vessels approaching the sharper bends in the Canal, particu-
larly when the next reach may be obscured, and all bends in Gaillard Cut, shall,
when at a distance of at least half a mile from such bend, slow down and blow
one prolonged blast as a notification to other vessels which may be c nuing
from the opposite direction; if there be no reply, the vessel may proceed, but
vessels shall not pass each other in the bends of the Canal; if there be a reply
to the first blast sounded, both vessels shall stop and proceed cautiously, follow-
ing the Rules of the Road, but the vessel which has the turn of the bend on her
port bow shall have the right to first proceed and make the turn.

clauses.label: Section 82.
clauses.text:
Section 82. When steam vessels are moving out from their docks or berths,
and other vessels are liable to pass from any direction toward them, the former
shall sound a prolonged blast, but immediately after clearing their berths so
as to be fully in sight, they shall be governed by the steering and sailing rules.

clauses.label: Section 83.
clauses.text:
Section 83. When steam vessels are running in the same direction, and the
vessel astern desires to pass on the starboard hand of the vessel ahead, she shall
give one short blast, and if the vessel ahead answers with one blast, they shall
maneuver accordingly; in case the vessel astern desires to pass on the port hand
of the vessel ahead (which, in the narrow waters of the Canal, is the habitual
and preferred practice), she shall give two short blasts of the whistle, to be
answered by the vessel ahead with two short blasts, and they shall maneuver
accordingly; but if the vessel ahead does not think it safe for the vessel astern
to attempt to pass at that point, she shall immediately give several short and
rapid blasts of the whistle, not fewer than four, and under no circumstances
shall the vessel astern attempt to pass the vessel ahead until such time as they
have reached a point where it can be safely done, when the vessel ahead shall
signify her willingness by blowing the proper signals; the vessel ahead shall in
no ease attempt to cross the bow or crowd upon the course of the passing
vessel.

clauses.label: Section 84.
clauses.text:
Section 84. Every vessel coming up with another vessel from any direction
more than two points abaft her beam shall be deemed to be an overtaking
vessel, and no subsequent alteration of the bearing between the two vessels
S

shall make the overtaking vessel a crossing vessel within the meaning of these
rules, or relieve her of the duty of keeping clear of the overtaken vessel until
she is finally passed and clear. If the overtaking vessel does not know with
certainty whether she is forward of or abaft this bearing from the other vessel,
she should, if in doubt, assume that she is an overtaking vessel and keep out
of the way.

clauses.label: Section 85.
clauses.text:
Section 85. Unless specially authorized by the Governor, no owner, master
or operator of floating craft, except such as may belong to or be chartered by
The Panama Canal, or such as may be in transit under charge of a Government
pilot, shall cause or permit such craft to enter, navigate or be present in Gaillard
Cut. Officers and agents of the Canal shall have power and authority to arrest
and take into custody, with or without process, any person or persons who may
violate this rule.

clauses.label: Section 86.
clauses.text:
Section 86. The movement of vessels in Gaillard Cut will be regulated by
the Port Captain, Balboa, through the signal stations and Pedro Miguel Locks.

clauses.label: Section 87.
clauses.text:
Section 87. Before passing a vessel, lighter, scow, dredger, pile driver or
anything that is afloat, whether moored, anchored or under way, vessels shall
slow down in plenty of time to pass at the slowest speed at which they can be
steered.

clauses.label: Section 88.
clauses.text:
Section 88. When in or near any lock a ship will, under no circumstances,
except in a sudden emergency, have a speed of more than two knots.

clauses.label: Section 89.
clauses.text:
Section 89. The following speeds shall not be exceeded by vessels in transit
through the Canal :
Knwts.
Colon to Gatun Locks......................... 6
Gatun Lake in the i,ooo-foot channels ............ 15
Gatun Lake in the Soo-foot channels .............. 12
Gatun Lake in the Soo-foot channels..............xo
Rounding Boblo and Darien bends ................ 6
Gaillard Cut ................................. 6
Rounding bends-Slowest speed at which steerageway can be maintained.
Miraflores Lake :
Vessels 360 feet or less in length and less than ao feet draft shall not cross
the Lake in less than 15 minutes.
Larger vessels shall not cross the Lake in less than 20 minutes.
Vessels of exceptional size or displacement shall not cross the Lake in less
than 25 minutes.
Knots.
Miraflores Locks to Pacific entrance of Canal .... 6
Entering or leaving port....................... 6

clauses.label: Section 90.
clauses.text:
Section 90. Under no condition will steamers be allowed to run side by
side in any part of the Canal waters, both going in the same direction, except for
the time necessary for one steamer to pass ahead of another, after the proper
signals have been made and answered. Should an occasion arise, however,
where steamers may find themselves running side by side, or nearly so, in the
same direction, in the open waters or elsewhere, the steamer on the right or star-
board side shall have the right of way, and the steamer on the left or port side
shall check her way, drop astern, and keep at a safe distance.

clauses.label: Section 91.
clauses.text:
Section 91. When two steamers are approaching each other at right angles
or obliquely so as to involve risk of collision, other than when one steamer is
overtaking another, the steamer which has the other on her port side shall hold
her course and speed ; and the steamer which has the other on her starboard side
shall keep out of the way of the other by directing her course to starboard so as
to cross the stern of the other steamer, or, if necessary to do so, slacken her speed,
or stop, or reverse. The steamer having the other on her own port bow shall
blow one blast of her whistle as a signal of her intention to cross the bow of the
other, holding her course and speed, which signal shall be promptly answered by
the other steamer by one short blast of her whistle as a signal of her intention to
direct her course to starboard so as to cross the stern of the other steamer or
otherwise keep clear.
9
11

clauses.label: Section 92.
clauses.text:
Section 92. If, from any cause whatever, the conditions covered by this
situation are such as to prevent immediate compliance with each others' signals,
the misunderstanding or objection shall at once be made apparent by blowing
the danger signal, and both steamers shall be stopped and backed, if necessary,
until signals for passing with safety are made and understood.

clauses.label: Section 93.
clauses.text:
Section 93. Where, by any of these rules, one of two vessels is to keep out
of the way, the other shall keep her course and speed.

clauses.label: Section 94.
clauses.text:
Section 94. Every vessiel which is directed by these rules to keep out of
the way of another vessel, shall, if the circumstances of the case permit, avoid
crossing ahead of the other and shall, on approaching her, if necessary, slacken
her speed, stop, or reverse.

clauses.label: Section 95.
clauses.text:
Section 95. When a steam vessel and a sailing vessel are proceeding in such
directions as to involve the risk of collision, the steam vessel shall keep out of
the way of the sailing vessel.

clauses.label: Section 96.
clauses.text:
Section 96. When two sailing vessels are approaching one another so as to
involve risk of collision, one of them shall keep out of the way of the other as
follows :

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) A vessel which is running free shall keep out of the way of a
vessel which is close-hauled.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) A vessel which is close-hauled on the port tack shall keep out
of the way of a vessel which is close-hauled on the starboard
tack.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) When both are running free, with the wind on different sides,
the vessel which has the wind on the port side shall keep out of
the way of the other.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) When both are running free with the wind on the same side,
the vessel which is to windward shall keep out of the way of the
vessel which is to leeward.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) A vessel which has the wind aft shall keep out of the way of the
other vessel.

clauses.label: Section 97.
clauses.text:
Section 97. Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, every
vessel overtaking another shall keep out of the way of the overtaken vessel.

clauses.label: Section 98.
clauses.text:
Section 98. Sailing vessels under way shall keep out of the way of sailing
vessels or boats fishing with nets, or lines, or trawls. This rule shall not give to
any vessel or boat engaged in fishing the right of obstructing a fairway used by
vessels other than fishing vessels or boats.

clauses.label: Section 99.
clauses.text:
Section 99. Nothing in these rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner
or master or crew thereof, from all the consequences of any neglect of any
precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the
special circumstances of the case.
Section ioo. In obeying or construing these rules, due regard shall be had
to all dangers of navigation and collision, and to any special circumstances
which may render a departure from the above rules necessary in order to avoid
immediate danger.
Section IoI. In fog, mist or heavy rainstorm, whether by day or night,
signals shall be given as follows:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) A steam vessel under way, except when towing other vessels or
being towed, shall sound, at intervals of not more than one
minute, on the whistle or siren, a prolonged blast.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) A vessel when towing other vessels shall sound, at intervals of
not more than one minute, on the whistle or siren, three blasts
in succession, namely: one prolonged blast followed by two short
blasts.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Seagoing dredges, when dredging, shall give four blasts in
succession: One prolonged blast followed by three short blasts.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) A vessel towed may give, at intervals of not more than one
minute, on the foghorn, a signal of three blasts in succession,
namely : One prolonged blast followed by two short blasts and
she shall not give any other.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) A sailing vessel under way shall sound, at intervals of not more
than one minute, when on the starboard tack one blast, when on
the port tack two blasts in succession, and when the wind is
abaft the beam three blasts in succession.
I0

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text:
(f) All rafts or other water craft, not herein provided for, navigated
by hand power, horsepower, or by the current of the river, shall
sound a blast on the foghorn, or- equivalent signal, at intervals
of not more than one minute.

clauses.label: (g)
clauses.text: (g) A vessel at anchor shall, at intervals of not more than oneminute, ring the bell rapidly for about five seconds.

clauses.label: Section 102.
clauses.text:
Section 102. Every vessel shall in fog, mist or heavy rainstorm, go at a
moderate speed, slow down, or stop, having due regard to the existing circum-
stances and conditions.

clauses.label: Section 103.
clauses.text:
Section 103. A steam vessel hearing, apparently forward of her beam, the
fog signal of a vessel the position of which is not ascertained, shall, as far as
circumstances of the case admit, stop her engines, and then navigate with cautionuntil the danger is over.

clauses.label: Section 104.
clauses.text:
Section 104. In thick and foggy weather vessels will not be allowed to
enter the Canal or leave the locks or mooring stations until the weather has
cleared. Vessels in transit, when overtaken by thick or foggy weather, must
immediately take every precaution and make preparation to anchor or moor at
the first available place, and so remain until the weather clears. Vessels
equipped with radio, when overtaken by thick or foggy weather, should immedi-
ately so report.i

clauses.label: Section 105.
clauses.text:
Section 105. Masters of vessels shall have prepared accurate tables showing
their compass error, before they will be allowed to enter the Canal. The general
direction of the Canal and its reaches is southeasterly and northwesterly, and
it would be well, if an opportunity offers, for vessels to obtain an accurate
deviation table on these courses, while in the approximate latitude and vicinity
of the Canal.
Section io6. Upon the first approach of thick weather of any kind, the
position of the ship must be accurately checked and the closest possible reckon-
ing be kept until the weather clears, or she shall have been moored or anchored.

clauses.label: Section 107.
clauses.text:
Section 107. Unnecessary sounding of the steam whistle is prohibited
within the waters of the Canal Zone; and any licensed officer in charge of a
steamer who authorizes or permits such unnecessary whistling may, upon
conviction thereof before a Board of Local Inspectors having jurisdiction,
be suspended from acting under his license.
Section io8. The word "visible" in these rules, when applied to lights,
shall mean visible on a dark night with a clear atmosphere.
Section io9. The rules concerning lights shall be complied with in all
weathers from sunset to sunrise, and during such time no other lights which
may be mistaken for the prescribed lights shall be exhibited.
Section i 10. A steam vessel when under way shall carry:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) On or in front of the foremast, or, if a vessel without a foremast,
then in the fore part of the vessel, a bright white light so con-structed as to show an unbroken light over an arc of the horizon
of 20 points of the compass, so fixed as to throw the light To
points on each side of the vessel, namely : From right ahead
to two points abaft the beam on either side, and of such a char-
acter as to be visible at a distance of at least five miles.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) On the starboard side a green light so constructed as to show
an unbroken light over an arc of the horizon of io points of
the compass, so fixed as to throw the light from right ahead to
two points abaft the beam on the starboard side, and of such
a character as to be visible at a distance of at least two miles.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) On the port side a red light so constructed as to show an unbroken
light over an arc of the horizon of i0 points of the compass, so
fixed as to throw the light from right ahead to two points abaft
the beam on the port side, and of such a character as to be
visible at a distance of at least two miles.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) The said green and red side lights shall be fitted with inboard
screens projecting at least three feet forward from the light, so
as to prevent these lights from being seen across the bow.
xi

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) On the stern a white light so constructed as to show astern over
an unbroken arc of twelve points, six points on each side of the
fore and aft line of the vessel. This light should be at about
the same height as the side lights and shall be visible for at least
one mile.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text:
(f) A seagoing steam vessel shall carry an additional white light
similar in construction to the light mentioned in subdivision (a).
These two lights shall be so placed in line with the keel that
one shall be at least 15 feet higher than the other, and in such
a position with reference to each other that the lower light
shall be forward of the upper one. The vertical distance of
these lights shall be less than the horizontal distance.
Section i I. A steam vessel when towing another vessel shall, in addition
to her side lights, carry two white lights in a vertical line, one over the other,
not less than three feet apart, and when towing more than one vessel, shall
carry an additional white light three feet above or below such lights, if the
length of the tow measuring from the stern of the towing vessel to the stern of
the last vessel towed exceeds 6oo feet. Each of the lights shall be of the same
construction and character, and shall be carried in the same position as the
white light described in Article i io (q).
Section i 12. A towing vessel may carry a small white light abaft the funnel,
aftermast, or at the stern, .r the vessel towed to steer by, but such light shall
not be visible forward of the beami.

clauses.label: Section 113.
clauses.text:
Section 113. A sailing vessel under way or vessel being towed shall carry
the red and green lights described in Article io (b) and (c). They shall never
carry the white lights described in Article 110o, but a sailing vessel which is being
overtaken by another vessel shall show from her stern to such last-mentioned
vessel a white light or a flare-up light.

clauses.label: Section 114.
clauses.text:
Section 114. Lights to be carried by motor boats are as follows:
Clas 1. (Les than(1) A white light aft to show all around the horizon.
26 ft. in length). (2) A combined lantern in the forepart of the vessel and lower
than the white light aft showing green to starboard and red
to port, so fixed as to throw the light from right ahead to two
points abaft the beam on their respective sides.
Classes II & III. (1) A bright white light in the fore part of the vessel as near the
(bu t.and oer
btlsthn6~ stem as practicable, so constructed as to show an unbrokenft.) light over an arc of the horizon of twenty points of the com-
pass, so fixed as to throw the light ten points on each side df
the vessel, namely, from right ahead to two points abaft the
beam on either side. The lens shall be of not less than the
following dimensions :
Class II: 19g square inches.
Class III. 31 square inches.
(2) A white light aft to show all around the horizon.

(3) On the starboard side a green light so constructed as to throw
an unbroken light over an arc of the horizon of ten points of
the compass so fixed as to throw the light from right ahead to
two points abaft the beam on the starboard side. On the
port side a red light so constructed as to show an unbroken
light over an arc of the horizon of ten points of the compass,
so fixed as to throw the light from right ahead to two points
abaft the beam on the port side. The lenses in the said side
lights shall be of not less than the following dimensions :
Class II: 16 square inches.
Class III : 25 square inches.
All lenses shall be fresnal or fluted. The said lights shall be
fitted with inboard screens of sufficient height and so set as
to prevent these lights from being seen across the bow and
shall be of not less than the following lengths:
Class I: 18 inches.
Class I: 24 inches.
Motor boats when propelled by sail and machinery or under
sail alone, shall carry the colored lights but not the white
lights presribed above.
12

Section 115~. Whenever, as in the case of vessels of less than ro gross tons
under way during bad weather, the red and green side lights can not be fixed,
these lights shall be kept at hand lighted and ready for use, and shall, on the
approach of or to c>her vessels be exhibited on their respective sides in sufficient
time to prevent collision, in such manner as to make them most visible, and so
that the green light shall not be seen on the port side nor the red light on the
starboard side, nor, if practicable, more than two points abaft the beam on
their respective sides. To make the use of these portable lights more certain
and easy, the lanterns containing them should each be painted outside with
the color of the light which they respectively contain, and shall be provided
with proper screens.
Section 11i6. Fishing vessels less than io gross tons, when under way, and
not having their nets, dredges or lines in the water, shall carry the usual white
light eight feet above the deck and shall have ready at hand a lantern with a
green glass on one side and a red glass on the other side, and on approaching
or being approached by another vessel, such lantern shall be exhibited in sufficient
time to prevent collision, so that the green light shall not be seen or he port tide
nor the red light on the starboard side.
Section 1 17. All fishing vessels and fishing boats of io gross tons or upward,
when under way and not having their nets, trawls, dredges, or lines in the water,
shall carry and show the same lights as other vessels under way.
Section i18. All vessels, when trawling, dredging or fishing, with any kind
of dragnets or lines, shall exhibit, from some part of the vessel where they can
be best seen, two lights. One of these lights shall be red and the other shall
be white. The red light shall be above the white light, and shall be at a vertical
distance from it of not less than 6 feet and not more than 1 2 feet; and the
horizontal distance between them, if any, shall be not more than 1o feet. These
two lights shall be of such a character and contained in lanterns of such con-
struction as to be visible all around the horizon, the white light at a distance
of not less than three miles and the red light not less than two miles.
Section i 19. A vessel under 150 feet in length when at anchor shall carry
forward, where it can best be seen, but at a height not exceeding 20 feet above the
hull, a white light, in a lantern constructed so as to show a clear, uniform and
unbroken light visible all around the horizon at a distance of at least one mile.

clauses.label: Section 120.
clauses.text:
Section 120. A vessel of 15o feet or upward in length when at anchor shall
carry in the forward part of the vessel, at a height of not less than 20 feet and
not exceeding 4o feet above the hull, one such light, and at or near the stern of
the vessel, and at such a height that it shall not be less than 15 feet lower than
the forward light, another such light.
Section 12 1. The length of the vessel shall be deemed to be the length
appearing in her certificate of registry.

clauses.label: Section 122.
clauses.text:
Section 122. Every vessel may, if necessary in order to attract attention,
in addition to the lights which she is by these rules required to carry, use a
flare-up light or use any detonating signal that cannot be mistaken for a distress
signal.

clauses.label: Section 123.
clauses.text:
Section 123. Every barge, lighter, canal boat, or scow that is moored
alongside of any ship or another barge, or to the side of the Canal, or to any
wharf, or lying at anchor on the navigable waters of the Canal zone, shall
show, between the hours of sunset and sunrise, a white light on the bow and
stern, at least three feet above the deck of said vessel, and not more than eight
feet from the bow and stern thereof.

clauses.label: Section 124.
clauses.text:
Section 124. Nothing in these rules shall interfere witi' the operation of
any special rules made by the government of any nation with respect to addi-
tional station and signal lights for two or more ships of war or for vessels sailing
under convoy, or with the exhibition of recognition signals adopted by ship-
owners, which have been authorized by their respective governments, and duly
registered and published, unless specific instructions are given by the Canal
authorities to discontinue the use of such lights while in transit through the
Canal.
r3

Section 1 25. Vessels propelled by machinery which are moored or anchoredshall display by day, forward where it can be best seen, one black ball or shapenot less than two feet in diameter.

clauses.label: Section 126.
clauses.text: Section 126. A steam vessel proceeding under sail only, but having herfunnel up, may carry in daytime, forward, where it can best be seen, one blackball or shape two feet in diameter.

clauses.label: Section 127.
clauses.text: Section 127. A vessel which from any accident is not under commandshall carry at the same height as the white light mentioned in Article i 1o (a),where they can best be seen, and if a steam vessel in lieu of that light, twored lights, in a vertical line one over the other, not less than six feet apart,and of such character as to be visible all around the horizon at a distance ofat least two miles; and shall by day ;:.1ry in a vertical line one over the other,not less than six feet apart, where they can best be seen, two black balls orshapes, each two feet in diameter.

clauses.label: Section 128.
clauses.text: Section 128. Seagoing suction dredges, when under way and dredging, shallcarry, besides the lights prescribed for steamers under way, between the twomasts where they can best be seen, two red lights approximately the sameheight as the masthead light of a steamer, in a vertical line one over the other,not less than six feet apart, and of such a character as to be visible all aroundthe horizon at a distance of at least two miles; and they shall, by day, carrybetween the two masts where they can best be seen, in a vertical line one overthe other, not less than six feet apart, two black balls or shapes, each two feetin diameter.

clauses.label: Section 129.
clauses.text: Section 129. Seagoing suction dredges, when dredging is stopped and thedredge is proceeding either to or from her dumping ground, either loaded orlight, shall, at night, extinguish the two red lights and, by day, lower the blackballs.

clauses.label: Section 130.
clauses.text: Section 130. Seagoing suction dredges, while actually engaged in dredging,as shown by the black balls, or red lights, shall have the right of way over allother vessels, but in the narrower reaches and in Gaillard Cut they shall giveway to seagoing ships. When not dredging, as shown by the absence of theblack balls or red lights, they shall observe all the Rules of the Road and haveno special privilege.

clauses.label: Section 131.
clauses.text: Section 131. Ferryboats, propelled by machinery and navigating the watersof the Canal Zone, shall carry the range lights and the side lights required bylaw to be carried on steam vessels.

clauses.label: Section 132.
clauses.text: Section 132. Barges, canal boats, scows, and lighters being towed astern ofsteam vessels, when towing singly or what is known as tandem towing, shalleach carry a white light on the bow and a white light on the stern.Section 133. When towed with a hawser two or more abreast, when in onetier, they shall carry a white light on the~ bow and a white light on the stern ofeach of the outside boats; when in more than one tier, each of the outside boatsshall carry a white light on its outer bow; and the outside boats in the last tiershall each carry, in addition, a white light on the outer after part of the stern.Section 134. Barges, etc., towed alongside a steam vessel, if on the starboardside of said steam vessel, shall display a white light on her own starboard bow,and if on the port side of said steam vessel, shall display a white light on her ownport bow; and if there he more ain one barge or canal boat alongside, the whitelight shall be displayed from the outboard side of the outside barge or canal boat.Section 135. Rafts propelled by hand power. or by the current of the riveror tide, or whuch shall be anchored in or near the channel or fairway, or proceedingin tow of a steam vessel, shall carry one white light on each corner of the raft.Section 136. Rowboats and cayucas, whether under oars or sail, shall carrya white light, visible all around the horizon, at an elevation above the surface ofthe water of at least three feet.

clauses.label: Section 137.
clauses.text:
Section 137. The white lights required by these rules for barges, canal boats,scows, lighters, rafts, rowboats and cayucas shall be visible all around the horizonat a distance of at least one mile. The lights for rafts shall be suspended so thatthey shall be not less than eight feet above the surface of the water.
t4

clauses.label: Section 138.
clauses.text:
Section 138. Any piece of floating equipment that is operated by means of
fore and aft, and side chains, shall carry, when the chains are taut, a black ball
on each side in some conspicuous place at least eight feet above the deck, and
near the positions of the side chains; at night these balls shall be replaced by a
red light and which shall show all around the horizon and be plainly visible at a
distance of at least one mile.

clauses.label: Section 139.
clauses.text:
Section 139. When a steamer wishes to pass any such equipment at a point
where it might foul its side chains, it should so signify by whistle signals, as
provided in these rules, and the piece of equipment concerned shall immediately
lower its chain on the side asked for by the steamer, indicating its fulfillment of
this by, in the daytime, lowering the ball, or, in the night, extinguishing the red
light.

clauses.label: Section 140.
clauses.text:
Section 140. If the craft is unable to lower its side chain, or should it
consider it dangerous for the steamer to pass on the side asked for, it will blow
the danger signal, when the steamer will stop until the ball is lowered or light
extinguished.

clauses.label: Section 141.
clauses.text:
Section 141. Any master or pilot of any steam vessel who shall flash, or
cause to be flashed, the rays of a searchlight into the pilot house of a passing
vessel shall be deemed guilty of misconduct and shall be liable to have his
license suspended or revoked; in general, searchlights shall not be used for
navigation purposes in transit through the Canal.

clauses.label: Section 142.
clauses.text:
Section 142. All vessels having a specially dangerous cargo, such as explo-
sives or oils of any kind shall fly a red flag at the masthead by day and show a
red light at night.
Section r43. When a vessel is in distress and requires assistance from
other vessels, or from the shore, the following shall be the signals to be used
or displayed by her, either together or separately, namely:
FIRST: Flames, as from a burning tar barrel, oil barrel, etc.
SECOND: A continuous sounding with any fog-signal apparatus, or firing
a gun.
THIRD: Rockets or shells showing stars, fired one at a time, at short
intervals.

clauses.label: Section 144.
clauses.text:
Section 144. In connection with these, vessels may use the international
code and special signals with shapes.

clauses.label: Section 145.
clauses.text:
Section 145. When lighters, barges, scows, or canal boats are to be moored
to any wharf, or along the shore in the channel in the navigable waters of the
Canal zone, they shall not be moored more than two deep.

clauses.label: Section 146.
clauses.text:
Section 146. Except in the terminal harbors or the authorized anchorages,
vessels shall not moor alongside one another in any part of the Panama Canal.
In the terminal harbors and authorized anchorages more than two vessels shall
not be moored alongside each other except by special permission of the Port
Captain and except that additional power hoists may be moored alongside two
vessels so connected, while actually engaged in transshipping cargo.

clauses.label: Section 147.
clauses.text:
Section 147. Nothing in the above rule shall be construed as affecting the
right of The Panama Canal to moor barges used in canal construction and
maintenance in any manner that may be deemed proper.

clauses.label: Section 148.
clauses.text:
Section 148. Every piece of floating equipment, except seagoing suction
dredges, that is engaged in excavating, or preparing to excavate in the Canal,
whose position is stationary, or moving from time to time over the face of the
shoal on which it is working, shall have the prior right to such position, and it
shall be unlawfu' for any person or persons, navigating a ship or otherwise, to
foul such equipment or its moorings in any way whatever.

clauses.label: Section 149.
clauses.text:
Section 149. All barges moved from berth to berth along wharves or banks
of the Canal shall be moved by a proper towboat. They shall not be moved
by hand power in the navigable fairway of the Canal, except to preserve life
or property in peril.
15

5. MISCELLANEOUS.
Section [50. While in a terminal port or in transit through the Canal no
vessel will be allowed to throw any~ ashes, cinders, ballast, solid matter of any
kind, boxes, paper, or anything that will float, heavy slops or anything that
will tend to deface or tend to make the waters of the Canal insanitary. This
does not apply to water-closet chutes, nor to the water used in cooking or in
cleaning tableware. Before arrival from sea at either terminal port, vessels
should dump ashes and get rid of all garbage, trash and slops.

clauses.label: Section 151.
clauses.text:
Section 151. Ships shall not pump engine or fireroom bilges while in Canal
zone waters or pump oil of any kind overboard.
Section 1 52. Ships alongside wharves shall not place any garbage on the
docks or wharves except in covered galvanized iron cans which are supplied
for that purpose. In case additional garbage cans are required, the Port Cap-
tain should be notified. Ships at docks desiring to land trash, such as boxes,
paper, sweepings, etc., can do so by requesting a dump car which will be put
alongside to receive such matter.

clauses.label: Section 153.
clauses.text:
Section 153. Vessels anchored or moored in the harbors for considerable
lengths of time may get rid of garbage of all kinds by requesting a garbage
scow to be put alongside.

clauses.label: Section 154.
clauses.text:
Section 154. No vessel shall make fast or run any lines to any marker,
buoy, beacon, or other aid to navigation. Vessels must use every precaution
to guard against injury to any of the aids to navigation in Canal waters; should
any damage or injury be inflicted, it shall be reported immediately to the Port
Captain.
Section 155 Vessels will he held liable for all damage done to the Canal
or any part of its plant or equipment. In case of the sinking in Canal waters
of any- floating or other equipment belonging to private persons or corporations
that creates or tends to create an obstruction, the Canal authorities may order
the removal of the obstruction at once, or remove it without waiting for action
by the owners and at the latters' expense.

clauses.label: Section 156.
clauses.text:
Section 156. Should a vessel go aground, collide, be in imminent danger,
or meet with any serious accident while in Canal waters, the Canal authorities
shall have the right to supervise and direct all operations in relation thereto,
that may be necessary to float her or clear the wreackage; but the master andall others under him, as well as every appliance on board the ship which may beof use, shall be placed at the disposal of the Canal authorities without additional
charge or claim against the Canal.

clauses.label: Section 157.
clauses.text:
Section 157. Vessels wishing to unload or load ballast must have proper
chutes, so arranged as to prevent ballast from falling overboard.

clauses.label: Section 158.
clauses.text:
Section 158. No warp or line shall be passed across any channel or dockso as to obstruct the passage of vessels or cause any interference with the dis-
charging of cargoes.

clauses.label: Section 159.
clauses.text: Section 159. Any damage caused by vessels or their mooring cables tothe works of any harbor will be repaired at the expense of the parties responsible.Section i6o. If a vessel occupying a berth at a wharf or pier, with or with-out the consent of the Port Captain, fails to vacate such berth when orderedby him; or when not loading or unloading, fails to make way for another vesselthat wishes to load or unload, the Port Captain shall then cause such vessel tobe moved to some other berth, and the expense of such removal shall be paidby the vessel, and in case of neglect or refusal to pay such expense upon demand,it may be recovered in an action before any court having jurisdiction.Section 161. Material of any kind, placed on any pier, bulkhead or otherproperty, must be removed therefrom within 36 hours, unless the Port Captainextends the time. All materials encumbering any pier, bulkhead or other prop-ert, after the time designated for the removal thereof shall have expired, willbe liable to be removed by the Port Captain to any warehouse or yard, at thesole risk and expense of the owner of such materials, and all expenses incurredfor such removal and storage, or otherwise, shall become a lien thereon, and suchmaterials will not be delivered to the owner until all expenses have been paid.

clauses.label: Section 162.
clauses.text:
Section 162. The owners, lessees, or occupants of any covered pier, wharf
or bulkhead, shall not use such pier, wharf, or bulkhead for the permanent
storage of material of any kind.

clauses.label: Section 163.
clauses.text:
Section 163. Covered piers, wharfs, and bulkheads are intended for the pro-
tection of merchandise and cargo in transit, and such merchandise and cargo
must be removed therefrom within 36 hours, unless the Port Captain may extend
the time. Any order to remove such material must be complied with promptly.

clauses.label: Section 164.
clauses.text:
Section 164. No fishing nets will be allowed in any place in the Canal, when-
ever in the opinion of the Marine Superintendent such nets interfere, or might
interfere, with navigation, and it shall be the duty of the owner thereof, upon
notification, to remove them immediately.

clauses.label: Section 165.
clauses.text:
Section 165. Anyone finding any buoy out of position, or lights not working
properly, should report it immediately to the Port Captain.

clauses.label: Section 166.
clauses.text:
Section 166. Steamers while within a Canal harbor must take all precau-
tions to avoid the issue of sparks or excessive smoke, and vessels will be held
liable for all damage resulting therefrom.

clauses.label: Section 167.
clauses.text:
Section 167. No pitch, tar, turpentine, or other combustible, shall be boiled
on any wharf, or on board any vessel without permission of the Port Captain.

clauses.label: Section 168.
clauses.text:
Section 168. In case of fire on board a vessel, all masters of other vessels
shall render such assistance as may be in their power.

clauses.label: Section 169.
clauses.text:
Section 169. A vessel anchored or moored in the harbor or lying at a dock
must at all times, night or day, have on board a sufficient number of men to
take care of the vessel.
Section 1 70. Ships at fueling berths must keep steam up and crew on board,
ready to move on short notice, unless special authority to the contrary has been
obtained beforehand from the Port Captain.
Section 17 1. No vessel shall unload lumber, timber, or piles into the waters
of a harbor without permission of the Port Captain, who shall designate where
such material shall be raf ted, nor shall any vessel tow a raft in the channel or
harbors of the Canal without such permission.

clauses.label: Section 172.
clauses.text:
Section 172. Lighters, barges, scows, and other vessels shall be anchored
in such places as the Port Captain may direct, and shall be at all times under
his supervision and direction.

clauses.label: Section 173.
clauses.text:
Section 173. It shall be unlawful for any person, without first having
secured a pilot's license from the Government of the Canal Zone, to navigate
in Canal Zone waters any steam vessel of more than 25 gross tons.

clauses.label: Section 174.
clauses.text:
Section 174. No privately owned craft may operate in Canal Zone waters
until those not propelled in whole or in part by machinery are registered and
numbered, and those propelled in whole or in part by machinery are registered
and ccrtiflcated. When numbers have been assigned, they shall be displayed
in a conspicuous place, in the prescribed form.

clauses.label: Section 175.
clauses.text:
Section 175. An applicant for a license to operate or navigate a motor
vessel of any type or tonnage shall pass a visual examination, unless he has
already been examined and granted a marine license by the Board of Local
Inspectors.
Section t 76. All sail boats, row boats, pangas, or cayucas carrying pas-
sengers in Canal Zone waters for which any compensation is collected, shall be
inspected annually and each such craft shall have its cubic capacity cut in the
hull in letters not less than x T/ inches high, and the paint over the letters shall
be of a different color from the other paint of the hull.

clauses.label: Section 177.
clauses.text:
Section 177. The number of persons to be carried by these boats shall be
determined by dividing the gross cubic foot capacity by 1 2 for all boats under
20 feet and by 10 for all boats 20 feet or over in length. All boats to carry a
life preserver for each passenger allowed.

clauses.label: Section 178.
clauses.text:
Section 178. All vessels moored to wharves, whether loading or unloading
cargo or in the ordinary way of business, shall be moored to the wharves with
rope hawsers only, and it shall he unlawful for any chain or wire hawsers to be
used on any public wharf in the Canal Zone without the specific permission of
the Port Captain.
17

clauses.label: Section 179.
clauses.text:
Section 179. All vessels, whether commercial or otherwise, moored to
wharves in the Canal zone, shall be compelled to keep watch at night and to
have suitable fire-fighting apparatus on hand.

clauses.label: Section 180.
clauses.text:
Section 180. Whenever it shall become necessary to remove any especially
inflammable cargo from ships at public wharves of the Canal Zone, the Port
Captain shall be notified at least two hours before such cargo shall be discharged
upon the wharf, so that proper means can be provided to dispose of this class
of material at the earliest possible moment.

clauses.label: Section 181.
clauses.text:
Section 181. No person or persons shall take possession of or use for any
purpose, make fast to or build upon, alter, deface, destroy, move or injure
any part of the plant or equipment, whether floating or otherwise, belonging
to the Canal.

clauses.label: Section 182.
clauses.text:
Section 182. Sailing directions for the Canal and approaches will be found
in Hydrographic Office Publications No. 174 South America Pilot, Volume III,
and No. 130, Central America and Mexico Pilot (East Coast).
II. PORT CAPTAINS.
1. GENERAL.

clauses.label: Section 183.
clauses.text:
Section 183. The Marine Division of the Department of Operation and Main-
tenance, in charge of the Marine Superintendent, is the organization in The Pan-
ama Canal through which all marine traffic and service to shipping are handled.
This division is represented at each terminal port by a Port Captain, who is
directly in charge of all such matters, and all local questions relating thereto
shall be referred to him.

clauses.label: Section 184.
clauses.text:
Section 184. Shipmasters can place themselves in direct touch with any
Canal utility, in whatever connection, most conveniently and promptly through
the Port Captains.

clauses.label: Section 185.
clauses.text:
Section 185. Every effort is made by The Panama Canal to expedite traffic
and to fill promptly the needs of shipping. Delays in getting in touch with
local facilities on arrival and in the necessary settlement of accounts prior to de-
parture are reduced to a minimum, but in this connection the active and intelli-
gent co-operation of shipmasters and local agents, as well as owners and operators,
is most essential and is earnestly solicited.

clauses.label: Section 186.
clauses.text:
Section 186. Masters can best assist by thoroughly familiarizing themselves
with the Canal Regulations and carrying them out, particularly as to the fol-
lowing:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Reporting accurately by radio, as far in advance as practicable,
the time of arrival; requirements; craft of ship; amount of local
cargo; number and class of local and through passengers, if any;
sanitary condition of vessel; sickness, if any, on board; number
and class of persons subject to quarantine detention, if any.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: (b) Assisting the boarding party in quickly carrying out their duties.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Advising the pilot accurately as to the maneuvering qualities and
peculiarities of the ship and of any defects.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text: (d) H-aing ship properly trimmed.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) Arriving, if possible, off the entrance in the early morning or fore-
nooE_.

clauses.label: Section 187.
clauses.text:
Section 187. Agents can materially assist by keeping the Port Captains in-
formed of the prospective arrival and requirements of their vessels, and by keep-
ing slips and their principals fully informed on all matters pertaining to the
Cana .

clauses.label: Section 188.
clauses.text:
Section 188. The co-operation of ship owners and operators is valuable in the
above particulars, both to themselves and to the Canal, and in this connection
their attention should be directed particularly to the load and trim of their ships,
the efficient condition of their motive machinery, steering gear, navigating and
piloting appurtenances, ground tackle, mooring lines, bitts and chocks; and the
efficiency of the personnel.

clauses.label: Section 189.
clauses.text:
Section 189. Information and supplies of Panama Canal printed forms can
readily be obtained from the Canal or from the Chief of Office, The Panama
Canal, Washington, D. C.
Is
2. SERVICES AND SUPPLIES.

clauses.label: Section 190.
clauses.text:
Section 190. Bunkers (coal, oil, Diesel oil, gasoline), lubricants, ships'
chandlery, fresh water suitable for drinking Atnd boiler use, engineering sup-
plies, every kind of fresh and dry provisions, meats, cold storage and dairy
products, ice, ice cream and fresh bakery products, can be obtained in any quan-
tity necessary for ship's use. Orders sent in advance by radio, cable, or mail,
can be delivered on arrival, and orders filed on arrival will be delivered promptly,
but in the case of ships transiting immediately, deliveries are made at the port
of departure. Docking is required only for bunkering.

clauses.label: Section 191.
clauses.text:
Section 191. Water in Gatun Lake between Gatun and Darien, is suitable
for boiler use, but not for drinking, and can be taken in by vessels during transit,
with the knowledge of the pilot, provided the trim of the ship is not altered
materially thereby or the ship delayed.

clauses.label: Section 192.
clauses.text:
Section 192. A steam laundry, available to ships and capable of doing any
kind of laundry work, is operated by the Canal. Laundry work sent ashore
from transiting ships in the early morning at entrance terminal will be done
and delivered at the departure terminal, without delaying the ship.

clauses.label: Section 193.
clauses.text:
Section 193. Tugs, for outside or Canal work, lighters and launches can be
obtained on application.

clauses.label: Section 194.
clauses.text:
Section 194. Dry docking and any kind of repairs or alterations for ships,
and their equipment, of any size and description are available. Requests for
such work can be made at any hour through the Port Captain, or to the Mechani-
cal Division direct. Any information desired on the subject can be obtained in
the same way. Work and information pertaining thereto should be requested
as far in advance as possible.

clauses.label: Section 195.
clauses.text:
Section 195. The duty on repairs done to American ships in foreign ports is
not applicable to such work done in the Canal Zone.

clauses.label: Section 196.
clauses.text:
Section 196. Repair and dry docking plants are in the hands of experts,
and work is done thoroughly and expeditiously and at moderate cost. In dry
docking, breakdowns are given preference over routine work and mail steamers
over cargo vessels.

clauses.label: Section 197.
clauses.text:
Section 197. Charges for dry docking commercial vessels are based on gross
tonnage for steam and motor vessels and net tonnage for sailing vessels, Panama
Canal measurement; for men of war charges are based on displacement.

clauses.label: Section 198.
clauses.text:
Section 198. Masters and officers of ships going into dry dock must fanuil-
iarize themselves with the " Rules for Docking Vessels in Dry Docks Belonging
to The Panama Canal. " These are furnished in pamphlet form.

clauses.label: Section 199.
clauses.text:
Section 199. In general, ships under repair are required to dock at the
repair wharves, but no wharf age is charged during actual repair work. Minor
repairs can be effected at commercial piers or at anchor.

clauses.label: Section 200.
clauses.text:
Section 200. All ships shall be fumigated immediately prior to going into
dry dock.

clauses.label: Section 201.
clauses.text: Section 201. Floating cranes up to a capacity of 250 tons are available.

clauses.label: Section 202.
clauses.text:
Section 202. A wrecking and salvage outfit, ready for immediate service,
is maintained for use at any point within a reasonable distance of the Canal.
Sec tion 203. The best of hospital service, medical and surgical, public and
private, is available to ships, and the only formality necessary to obtain hospital
treatment is, in the case of American seamen, a master's certificate, and for
foreign seamen, a letter of identification, assuming responsibility for hospital
charges.'

clauses.label: Section 204.
clauses.text:
Section 204. Canal physicians will visit ships on application to the Port
Captain or to the nearest hospital or dispensary.

clauses.label: Section 205.
clauses.text:
Section 205. In cases of emergency, free medical advice may be obtained
by ships at sea by radio from The Panama Canal, through the radio stations at
Colon, Balboa, or Cape Mala. Such message should be addressed: "Govt.
C.B., Medico, Pancanal," state briefly and clearly the symptoms to be treated,
and be signed by the master.
19

clauses.label: Section 206.
clauses.text:
Section 206. The accuracy of~ the advice given is not guaranteed nor will
any responsibility be assumed by The Panama Canal or medical authorities
thereof, in this connection. Neither will The Panama Canal nor the radio
stations guarantee the accuracy of the transmission of such messages. However,
every effort is made to give valuable advice quickly and accurately.

clauses.label: Section 207.
clauses.text:
Section 207. No receiving or sending charge is imposed by the short stations
for this service and ships should make none.

clauses.label: Section 208.
clauses.text:
Section 208. Duly authorized notaries public for the Canal Zone are em-
ployed in the offices of the Port Captains.

clauses.label: Section 209.
clauses.text:
Section 209. Branches of the U. S. Hydrographic Office are maintained in
the Port Captains' offices, where every description of hydrographic and meteoro-
logic information is obtainable gratis.

clauses.label: Section 210.
clauses.text: Section 210. Charts and sailing directions are for sale.

clauses.label: Section 211.
clauses.text: Section 211. Chronometer and barometer comparisons are obtainable gratis.

clauses.label: Section 212.
clauses.text:
Section 212. Charges for service and supplies are published and furnished to
all interested parties, who should keep posted up to date on current tariffs and
price lists, which are subject to change without notice.

clauses.label: Section 213.
clauses.text:
Section 213. Annual contracts for supplies and services to shipping will not
be entered into by the Canal.

clauses.label: Section 214.
clauses.text:
Section 214. The payment of bills for all services rendered by the Canal
or Panama Railroad shall be made to the Collector of The Panama Canal at either
Cristobal or Balboa; except that deposits to cover tolls and other bills may be
made with the Treasurer of the United States or with a Federal Reserve Bank
in the United States to the credit of the Collector, in lieu of cash on the Isthmus.
All payments in cash must be made in United States currency.

clauses.label: Section 215.
clauses.text:
Section 215. All charges to he incurred must lie covered by deposits of
funds before service will be rendered or supplies furnished, and all bills must be
settled in full before a vessel will be allowed to clear.

clauses.label: Section 216.
clauses.text:
Section 216. Bills for supplies and services of all kinds will he submitted
to the Collector by the department furnishing supplies or rendering services.
Those for supplies or services to ships of established lines with agencies on the
Isthmus, will be submitted to local agents if so desired.

clauses.label: Section 217.
clauses.text:
Section 217. The most satisfactory way of prepaying tolls and other charges
is by deposit with a Federal Reserve Bank in the United States, which should
be requested to cable the Isthmus immediately, giving the amount of the deposit,
the ship for which it is made, and the name of the depositor. The cost of this
cable service is $s and the amount is charged against the deposit. It is recom-
mended that the deposit be slightly more than sufficient to cover tolls and other
t charges, so that in case the latter exceed the amount anticipated the vessel
j need not be delayed. It is also well to make the deposit several days in advance
of the vessel's expected arrival in Canal waters, in order that she may not be held
pending receipt of notice of deposit.
Section 21iS. As soon as possible after the ship has passed through the Canal
the total amotmt chargeable against the vessel is deducted from the amount of
the deposit and a statement of the account is sent to the depositor. Any unex-
pended balance is remitted to the depositor with the statement, except where
it is desired to apply the balance on charges against other vessels.

clauses.label: Section 219.
clauses.text:
Section 219. A shipping firm having offices in a port where there is a Federal
Reserve Banak can make its deposits direct, while those whose offices are else-
where, or in foreign countries, can remit through their bankers or through other
shipping agencies. Those sending vessels through the Canal at frequent inter-
vals, may make a lump sum deposit dnd keep an open account with The Panama
Canal, but should specify by name the vessels to which such deposit is to apply.
3. ADMPASURtMENT.

clauses.label: Section 220.
clauses.text:
Section 220. Vessels shall provide themselves with the proper tonnage
certificate, based upon the rules laid down for Panama Canal measurement.
1~Section 221. In addition to the admeasurers at the Canal, the CollectorsF of Customs in the large seaport cities of the United States, and certain properly
designated officials abroad, have been authorized to measure vessels under The
I

Panama Canal rules and issue the required certificate. In case a vessel is not so
provided, she should have a full set of plans and a copy of the measurements
which were made when she received her national tonnage certificate, and also the
tonnage certificate itself.

clauses.label: Section 222.
clauses.text:
Section 222. Vessels which have not been measured arriving at the Canal
for transit will be measured before transiting, with consequent delay and at a
charge of $50 each.

clauses.label: Section 223.
clauses.text:
Section 223. The rules for the measurement of vessels will be found in the
Proclamation of the President of the United States, dated November 21, 1913.

clauses.label: Section 224.
clauses.text:
Section 224. The admeasurers at the Canal must know the United States
net registered tonnage, or the equivalent thereof and The Panama Canal net
tonnage of every vessel arriving for transit. Tolls are based on net tonnage,
and the rates will be found in the " Panama Canal Tariff".

clauses.label: Section 225.
clauses.text:
Section 225. Under all conditions, the Canal authorities res'xrve the right
to check and correct any measurement or certificate issued elsewhere.

clauses.label: Section 226.
clauses.text:
Section 226. In order for vessels "in ballast without passengers or cargo"
to benefit by the reduced rate for toll charges, they must not have on board fuel
in excess of the volume deducted on their Panama Canal Tonnage Certificates
(Page 2, item I (b) or 2 (b) under Propelling Power Deduction) for bunker
space. For convenience this volume is converted into long tons and placed at
the bottom of page 2 on all certificates issued, checked or corrected at the Canal.
4. ACCIDENTS, DUFECTh AND CLAIMS.

clauses.label: Section 227.
clauses.text:
Section 227. No claim against The Panama Canal for damages on account
of injury to a vessel or its cargo while in Canal Zone waters, arising from the
operation of the Canal otherr than the passing of the vessel through the locks)
shall be allowed, unless it shall be determined by the Governor of The Panama
Canal that such injury was due to the negligence or want of care on the part of
agencies or employees of The Panama Canal.

clauses.label: Section 22S.
clauses.text:
Section 22S. In case a vessel, or its passengers or cargo, meets with an
accident or sustains any damage which may be the basis of any claim against
The Panama Canal, it shall be reported immediately to the Port Captain, who
will refer it to the Board of Local Inspectors, and the Board, or a member
thereof, shall hold an investigation as soon as possible.

clauses.label: Section 229.
clauses.text:
Section 229. The Board of Local Inspectors, or any member thereof, has
authority to summon and administer oaths to witnesses, and the attendance of
witnesses may be compelled by court process, on application of the Board to
the District Judge.

clauses.label: Section 230.
clauses.text:
Section 230. The findings of the Board are submitted in writing to the
Governor, through the Marine Superintendent, for the Governor's approval,
after which an adjustment will be made. Interested parties will be furnished a
copy of the report when requested.

clauses.label: Section 231.
clauses.text:
Section 231. All matters pertaining to such an investigation shall be com-
pleted before the vessel concerned leaves Canal waters, and no claim will be
considered unless the reason thierefor has been laid before the Canal authorities
prior to the vessel's sailing.

clauses.label: Section 232.
clauses.text:
Section 232. All claims for damages arising from injury to vessels, cargo, or
passengers, from the passing of vessels through the locks, shall be adjusted by
mutual agreement, when practicable, between The Panama Canal and the pas-
sengers, owners, agents, or underwriters of the vessel, or owners, agents or
underwriters of the cargo of the vessel, as the respective interests may appear.
In case of disagreement, suit may be brought by the claimant in the District
Court of the Canal Zone, against the Governor of The Panama Canal.

clauses.label: Section 233.
clauses.text:
Section 233. Settlement of claims for damages to vessels may include the
actual or estimated cost of repairs, charter hire actually lost by the owners, or
charter hire actually paid by the charterers of a vessel, depending on the terms of
the charter pkirty, for the time a vessel is tied up undergoing repairs necessitated
by an injury for which The Panama Canal is found liable.
21

clauses.label: Section 234.
clauses.text:
Section 234. If the maintenance of the vessel and wages of the crew are
shown to be actually additional expenses or losses incurred outside of charter
hire, they may be included as a part of the damages chargeable to The Panama
Canal.

clauses.label: Section 235.
clauses.text:
Section 235. Settlement may include other expenses, not including agents'
fees, commissions or other incidental expenses of a similar nature, which are
definitely and accurately shown to have been necessarily incurred by reason of
the accident for which The Panama Canal is liable.

clauses.label: Section 236.
clauses.text:
Section 236. If a vessel is not operated under charter, but by the owner
personally, evidence shall be secured, if available, as to the sum for which vessels
of the same size and class can be chartered in the market. If unable to determine
such charter value, the value of the use of such vessel to her owner in the business
in which she was engaged at the time of the injury shall be used as a basis for
estimating the damage for the vessel's detention, and the books of the owner
showing the vessel's net earnings about the time of the accident shall be con-
sidered as evidence of probable earnings during the time of detention. If the
books are unavailable, such other evidence shall be furnished as may be required
by the Auditor.

clauses.label: Section 237.
clauses.text:
Section 237. The Auditor shall be furnished with such vouchers, receipts
or other evidence as may be required by him in support of any item of a claim.

clauses.label: Section 238.
clauses.text:
Section 238. No items which are speculative, indefinite, indeterminable, or
matters of conjecture shall be allowed.

clauses.label: Section 239.
clauses.text:
